annotations.description: The witness re-cosigns every log it polls at least hourly, so this means THE WITNESS is stuck, not that a log is quiet. While stale, equivocation on that log would go undetected — the cosignature timestamp is what consumers use to tell a live witness from a dead one. Push-only logs (tier "A (checkpoint witness, pushed)") are excluded: they are cosigned only when their operator pushes, so their staleness measures the operator, not us; "a push-only log has gone quiet" covers them. Check: docker compose logs on docker-services, and http://192.168.0.146:8088/
annotations.summary: A log the witness polls has not been cosigned in over two hours.

model.query:
from(bucket: "server")
  |> range(start: -15m)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r.stack == "kt-witness" and r._field == "kt_witness_log_staleness_seconds" and r.tier != "A (checkpoint witness, pushed)")
  |> max() |> group() |> max() |> keep(columns: ["_value"])

title: kt-witness: a push-only log has gone quiet

annotations.summary: A witness-network log that only pushes to us has not pushed in over a day.
annotations.description: Not a witness fault: a push-only log is cosigned only when its operator sends a checkpoint, and this one has stopped. Find it on /metrics (kt_witness_log_staleness_seconds with the pushed tier). If it publishes at https://<origin>/, the hourly probe will start polling it on its own (witness_network.poll); otherwise the operator's contact is on the list and on /graph. NoData is OK: with no push-only logs there is nothing to report.

model.query:
from(bucket: "server")
  |> range(start: -15m)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r.stack == "kt-witness" and r._field == "kt_witness_log_staleness_seconds" and r.tier == "A (checkpoint witness, pushed)")
  |> max() |> group() |> max() |> keep(columns: ["_value"])
